text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS
- President Lennart Meri opened new schoolhouse in Kolkja, near Lake Peipsi.
- The election of professors to Tartu University led to a row between the candidates.
SONUMILEHT
- Both Tallinn and Stockholm are competing about the right to house the Baltic Sea Countries Council secretariat.
- Prime Minister Mart Siimann met representatives of pensioners. He promised to link the subsistence support to CPI and to review the resolution on the payment of welfare sums.
- A U.S. coast guard cutter Legare participated in a joint exercise with Estonian border guard yesterday.
EESTI PAEVALEHT
- The mother of a test tube baby wants the state to pay for the in-vitro fertilisation. The sum claimed from her is 2,900 kroons.
- Estonian Foreign Minister Toomas Hendrik Ilves called for closer economic cooperation at the Baltic Sea Countries Council session in Riga.
- Interior Minister Robert lepikson approved the new statutes of the Police Department, which increases its power in the control of the police.
POSTIMEES

- The prisons department claims that the building of a special "European"-style block for life prisoners would cost taxpayers 38 million kroons. One life prisoner would cost the nation 7,700 kroons per month.
- Former Estonian ambassador to Lithuania, Valve Strikaitiene, received Lithuanian citizenship from President Algirdas Brazauskas.
- More artillery shells were found in the island of Naissaar. The latest search revealed a total of 740, but there may be more and the defence forces warn tourists to take care.
ARIPAEV
- Tallinna Pank will buy the Latvian Saules Banka. All shares will be purchased by the end of the year.
- Nordika insurance form will be the largest in Estonia after increasing its share capital to 60 million kroons.
- Economic experts have rated Estonia's current economic state the best in the last two years and predict it to continue in the nearest six months.
